result.topic_en: Gauss reformulates the requirements for a general solution of a problem (apparently about rational values of quantities α', β, γ', δ, ε') as finding four numbers p, q, P, Q such that (pp−qq)(PP−QQ) and pqPQ are squares; he gives expressions for the quantities, a transformation producing a second solution from a first, and a trigonometric parametrisation.
result.transcription:
Das zu einer allgemeinen Auflösung erforderliche
kann man auch so einkleiden; suchet 4 Zahlen $p, q.$ $P, Q$
so dass
$(pp-qq)(PP-QQ)$ Quadrate werden
und $pqPQ$
Dann ist
$\alpha'$ | $\sqrt{\frac{qQ}{pP}}$
$\beta$ | $\sqrt{\frac{qP}{pQ}}$
$\gamma'$ | [-$\sqrt{\frac{pq}{PQ}}$ $\sqrt{\frac{rr}{pp-ss}}$-] $\sqrt{\frac{pq}{PQ}}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{PP-QQ}{pp-qq}}$
$\delta$ | $\sqrt{\frac{p+q}{p-q}\cdot\frac{P-Q}{P+Q}}$
$\varepsilon'$ | $\sqrt{\frac{p-q}{p+q}\cdot\frac{P-Q}{P+Q}}$
und aus Einer Auflösung folgt eine zweite
anstatt
$p$ | $ppPP-qqQQ$
$q$ | $ppQQ-qqPP$
$P$ | $(pp+qq)PQ+(PP+QQ)pq$
$Q$ | $(pp+qq)PQ-(PP+QQ)pq$
anstatt
$p+q$ | $(pp-qq)(PP+QQ)$
$p-q$ | $(pp+qq)(PP-QQ)$
$P+Q$ | $2(pp+qq)PQ$
$P-Q$ | $2(PP+QQ)pq$
Sind $p, q :: \cos m, \sin m$
$P, Q :: \cos M, \sin M$
so ist proportional
$p'$ .... $\cos M-m \cos M+m$   $p'+q'$ $\cos 2m$
$q'$ ..... $\sin M-m, \sin M+m$   $p'-q'$ $\cos 2M$
$P'$   $\cos M-m \sin M+m$   $P'+Q'$ $\sin 2M$
$Q'$   $\cos M+m \sin M-m$   $P'-Q'$ $\sin 2m$

methods.what: Expressions of the quantities α', β, γ', δ, ε' in terms of p, q, P, Q
Transformation generating a second solution from a given one
Sums and differences of the new solution values (alternative 'anstatt' form)
Trigonometric parametrisation p:q = cos m : sin m, P:Q = cos M : sin M, giving the new solution in terms of angles M±m
